questions.q: What should determine which visual you pick, according to this lesson?
options: The question you're trying to answer with the data
Which visual icon looks the most sophisticated
Whichever visual is listed first in the Visualizations pane
The total number of columns in your table
questions.explain: Starting from the question — comparison, trend, part-to-whole, exact values, or a single key number — leads to the visual actually built to answer it.

questions.q: Which visual is best suited for showing a trend over a continuous time axis?
options: A line chart
A pie chart
A card
A slicer
questions.explain: Line charts emphasize the overall shape of change over time, which is exactly what a trend question calls for.

questions.q: Why might a treemap be a better choice than a pie chart for some part-to-whole data?
options: A pie chart falls apart with many categories, while a treemap handles a much larger number using nested rectangle sizes
Treemaps only work with numeric axes
Pie charts can't show percentages
Treemaps are required whenever there's more than one measure
questions.explain: Pie and donut charts work best with a small number of slices. Treemaps scale to many more categories by representing value through rectangle size instead of slice angle.

questions.q: When should you reach for a table or matrix instead of a chart?
options: When the audience needs to see and compare precise, exact numbers rather than a visual impression
Whenever there's more than one column of data
Only when the report has no measures
Tables should never be used in a polished report
questions.explain: Charts communicate a visual impression of data; tables and matrices are for when exact values matter more than shape or pattern.

questions.q: What's the difference between a card and a KPI visual?
options: A card highlights a single measure; a KPI visual shows that measure's progress toward a specific target
A card can show unlimited measures; a KPI can only show one
KPI visuals can't be filtered; cards can
There is no difference — they're interchangeable
questions.explain: Cards put one number front and center. KPI visuals go further, adding a target and showing how close the current value is to reaching it.
